dedupe_keys.name: corralanna peatland high frequency storm flow series 2021 2023

description: This flow dataset complements storm-water chemistry measurements from the Corralanna cutaway peatland catchment in Ireland. University College Dublin and Teesside University researchers monitored fourteen storms between March 2021 and March 2023 using area-velocity and bubbler instruments. The recorded interval ranges from one to five minutes, covering rising, peak and recession phases. Mendeley version 2 supplies one Excel workbook free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is a single 16.4-hectare industrial peatland drainage outlet, with six storms below fifteen litres per second at peak and eight above thirty. Event-based coverage and water-level conversion through a rating curve are limitations for treating these traces as complete annual discharge. Modellers could calibrate drainage hydrographs or supply time-varying flow to treatment and pollutant-transport simulations. model-epa-swmm and platform-goldsim-mine-water-waste are related modelling tools. The flow and chemistry releases share events and should not be counted as independent campaigns. No hydrograph was downloaded or rating curve checked.
